# The Last Train

The station was empty except for a woman in a green coat and a dog that did not belong to anyone. She had missed the last train by four minutes, and the clock above the platform seemed pleased about it.

"You can wait in the office," said the stationmaster. "The heater works, mostly."

She thanked him and stayed where she was. The rails hummed with something far away, a train that was not coming here, and she listened to it until the sound became part of the night.

The dog lay down at her feet. She shared half a sandwich with it, then the other half, and laughed at herself for being so easily persuaded.

At midnight the stationmaster came out with two cups of tea. They drank in silence, watching the signal lights change from red to green and back again for trains that never arrived.

When the first morning train finally pulled in, she stood, brushed the crumbs from her coat, and looked down at the dog. It looked back. She sighed, opened the door, and they climbed aboard together.
